messages:
jordan: Quick sync 10. We need a clear visibility contract for errors before we flip the console beta. Questions: which fields are allowed in client responses, what belongs only to internal traces, and what SDKs should treat as authoritative. Also: SLA wording might need to change depending on public codes.

tara: Proposal (short): public surface = {status_bucket, user_message, retry_hint}. Internal-only = {internal_reason, node_id, target_model, kv_state}. Keep internal values in traces and in `X-Redwood-Subcode` header but mark them explicitely opaque.

ben: For HTTP semantics: map buckets to codes like: OK -> 200, rate_limit -> 429, blocked -> 403 (for auth/entitlement), soft_degraded -> 503, hard_internal -> 500. Reason: 503 signals transient so clients/backends can backoff.

mei: Can we standardize `retry_hint` values? I suggest `immediate|short_wait|contact_support`. Also include `Retry-After` header when we have a TTL known. Avoid free-form text in headers.

sophie: Console UX note: show a nice human string in the UI not the `subcode`. Example: "Model unavailable briefly; we'll keep trying."

jordan: Example response (minimal):
```http
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Status: soft_degraded
X-Redwood-Subcode: model_warmup.v3
X-Redwood-Retry-Hint: short_wait
Retry-After: 5
{
  "error": {
    "code": "soft_degraded",
    "user_message": "Temporary slowdown, please retry in a few seconds.",
    "retry_hint": "short_wait"
  }
}
```

ben: +1 to including Retry-After. Important: subcodes must never be part of billing or entitlement checks on client side. Opaque.

mei: Telemetry plan: emit both public and internal fields to ingest pipeline. For cost reasons, full internal_reason is sampled at 1% by default per tenant, but when an internal_reason spikes above 0.5% of errors we switch that tenant to full-capture for 30 minutes. Alerting: fire pager if a tenant has >5% of requests hitting the same internal_reason for 10m.

tara: Rollout steps: (1) telemetry only (add subcodes to traces), (2) beta headers for selected customers, (3) enable headers for all with opt-out. Each step must include 2-week canary and synthetic checks for retry behavior.

ops-bot: deployment: gateway/status-headers rolled to canary group (5/60) 1061239076

sophie: SDK policy: default SDK behavior should NOT retry on `hard_internal` or `blocked`. For `soft_degraded` we can retry up to 3 times with backoff, but respect `Retry-After` / `retry_hint`. Document this prominently. Also include an opt-in `aggressiveRetries` flag for advanced users.

jordan: Legal/SLA check: if we expose `soft_degraded` widely we must ensure it's not interpreted as SLA breach automatically. Ops and legal to agree on language in docs: "soft_degraded is transient and not an SLA violation unless sustained > X minutes."

ben: Implementation note: gateway will add `X-Redwood-Subcode` and `X-Redwood-Retry-Hint` behind a feature flag. Console will default to showing only `status_bucket` unless tenant toggles reveal mode.

mei: Metrics team: we'll add a dashboard tile that correlates subcodes -> latency/p99/failure-rate and a per-tenant heatmap. I'll draft the dashboard and share by EOD.

tara: Runbook owners: Jordan draft the mapping table + FAQ (due EOD). Ben own gateway flag PR. Mei own telemetry sampling rule. Sophie own SDK PR. Ops-bot will announce canary progress.

jordan: One more: please avoid using `500` for all internal problems. Where possible prefer `503`/`429` to guide client behavior. We'll note mapping in the RFC.

ops-bot: alert: canary hosts show small uptick in `model_warmup.v3` (15 events in last 2m) 1061239070

ben: thanks. I'll bump the synthetic test to include 429 and 503 handling and run it across canary.

jordan: Great. We'll reconvene 9:30am to sign off on wording before docs publish. Thanks everyone :rocket:
